ud3.7:2.3: As told at Ud 1.6:2.3, Kassapa refused alms from the gods and visited poor areas, such as the streets of the embroiderers.
ud3.7:3.2: The pesa was evidently gold-embroidered cloth. Of old, Indra was known for bearing gifts of such cloth (Rig Veda 1.61.16, 1.63.9). Here he is making pesa together with his wife Sujā (SN 11.12:6.1). She spins the thread, while he embroiders the patterns. | The Pali’s tantaṁ (“thread”) here echoes the verb tanute (“one threads”) said of the peśaskārī at Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 4.4.4, confirming that it is the same action described. There, one is said to embroider a figure such as a person.
ud3.7:3.6: I’m not sure if anekarasabyañjano is correct, although the word does occur at Pv 13:15.4 and Pv 27:12.4. The commentary, while not definitive, suggests anekasūpabyañjano (anekehi sūpehi ceva byañjanehi ca), which would be more idiomatic. However it is not attested.
